title: SciWorkBench: A Benchmark for Real Scientific Workflows
abstract: arXiv:2611.22490v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language models are increasingly being used as agents capable of planning and executing projects, as well as refining their actions through feedback. This shift raises a question: can current agents complete projects like real scientists? To examine this question, we introduce SciWorkBench, a benchmark for evaluating agents' abilities on real science tasks across biology, chemistry, materials science, and physics. SciWorkBench is built from peer-reviewed literature or expert-contributed research scenarios. We also propose a unified scientific analysis framework validated by domain experts, which can categorize most tasks in SciWorkBench. Each task covers one or more stages of this framework. We evaluate up-to-date models within the Claude Code and Codex agent frameworks under a unified execution and grading protocol. translated_title: SciWorkBench：面向真实科学工作流的基准测试
translated_abstract: 语言模型正越来越多地被用作能够规划和执行项目、并通过反馈改进自身行动的智能体。这一转变引出了一个重要问题：当前的智能体能否完成像真实科学家那样的项目？为了研究这个问题，我们提出了SciWorkBench，一个用于评估智能体在真实科学任务上能力的基准，涵盖生物学、化学、材料科学和物理学等领域。SciWorkBench基于同行评审文献或专家贡献的研究场景构建。我们还提出了一个经领域专家验证的统一科学分析框架，可以对SciWorkBench中的大多数任务进行分类，每个任务涵盖该框架的一个或多个阶段。我们在统一的执行和评分协议下，在Claude Code和Codex智能体框架内评估了最新模型。表现最好的智能体平均得分为57.38，这表明当前的智能体在完成真实科学任务方面仍然存在明显困难。
tldr: 本文提出SciWorkBench——一个基于同行评审文献和真实科研场景构建的基准，用于评估AI智能体在生物、化学、材料科学和物理等真实科学任务上的能力，结果表明即使是表现最好的智能体平均得分也仅为57.38分，说明现有智能体完成真实科学工作仍有显著差距。
en_tdlr: SciWorkBench is a new benchmark built from peer-reviewed scientific literature and expert-contributed scenarios to evaluate AI agents on real scientific tasks across biology, chemistry, materials science, and physics, revealing that even the best-performing agents (mean score 57.38) still struggle with realistic scientific workflows.
